subject: alebrije
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: alebrije jaguar-eagle.
Style: Oaxacan alebrije painted wood.
reasoning:
I'm designing a jaguar-eagle alebrije hybrid: a jaguar body with an eagle's beaked, crested head, feathered wings, and a tail painted with dots, all finished in the bright zigzag and spiral patterns typical of alebrije folk art.

I'm planning the skeleton with hip, spine, neck, head, jaw, tail, leg, and wing joints sized for a jaguar-scale body, then setting a bold palette of turquoise, magenta, yellow, orange, green, deep blue, white, and black with custom rosette-spot and countershaded paint patterns for the fur and feathers. Now I'm working out the sweep geometry for the spine chain to form the body shape.

Head joint placed at the neck's end with a slight downward tilt, and I'm shaping the eagle skull as a scaled sphere with a hooked upper beak swept from the front of the head using a bezier curve.

For the eyes, I'm using small textured circles placed on the sides of the head angled slightly forward, positioning them just outside the skull ellipsoid surface so they sit nested against it rather than floating.

Now for the crest, I'm planning a fan of extruded feather shapes arranged along the top of the head, using a leaf-like outline for each feather.

I want to add round jaguar-style ears to the eagle head as spheres with inner coloring, plus brow ridges and a ring of decorative dots around the eye using small spheres oriented outward along the eye's rim.

Now moving to the legs: I'm positioning the front leg joints with shoulder and foot coordinates, then checking the reach distance against the max leg length to make sure the limb can actually extend that far.

For the feet I'm giving the legs sphere paws with eagle-style talons, spawning three spike toes forward from each foot tip joint with slight splay and curvature for a clawed look.

Now I'm checking the vertical positioning so the paws and toes rest at the correct ground height, then moving on to sketch the wings extending from the shoulders outward and upward in a display-spread pose.

Working out the wing joint chain and feather placement...

Still working out feather orientation...

Placing the feather extrudes along the wing chain path at sampled positions, using 8 primaries and 6 coverts per side for 28 total. For the body, I'm adding decorative dot rows along the spine sweep and sides using stick placements sampled from the sweep surface.

Still writing paint design...

Adding tail tip plume with fanned feathers for the eagle look, then moving to head coloring: a white-cream bald eagle style with blue/turquoise top and a dotted helper function for mottled yellow spots.

Now I'm figuring out a feathered neck ruff using a ring of outward-leaning feather cards around the neck base, adjusting tilt and spacing so they flare backward like a collar.

Adding decal placements...

Still writing beak geometry...

I'll skip cere and tongue details since this is an eagle-style hooked beak, and move to defining the head joint, which needs to attach to the end of the neck chain. I'm setting up the neck path with a few control points leading up to where the head joint sits.

Now I'm defining the hips as the root joint and starting the spine chain from there, then working out a belly-shaped radius function along the body that tapers smoothly for the sweep profile.

For the spine I'm setting up a 4-point path split into 3 segments, auto-naming each joint spine1 through spine3, with the chest front shaped by a wider sine-based radius curve. Then I'm sketching a tail chain of 4 joints branching from the hips, tapering the radius toward the tip, and considering how to fan out feather shapes from the tail's endpoint.

I'm working out the direction vectors for the fanned feathers at the tail tip, placing five of them spaced at 25-degree increments, and defining a feather helper function that extrudes each one with a given anchor point, direction, thickness, and color.

Now I'm defining the outline shape for each feather as a tapered leaf-like polygon with sharp tip and base points, and setting up a paint function that applies an accent color near the feather's quill line and around a central dot pattern.

I'm thinking through caching strategy: paints keyed by base/accent/length so I don't regenerate identical paint functions, with two length variants for primaries versus coverts, and roughly a dozen total paints across color cycles plus tail feathers.

For the feather direction math, I'm working out how primaries should hang from the wing's trailing edge — falling back and slightly downward, fanning more outward toward the tip — and normalizing a direction vector from the span parameter, then picking a perpendicular axis for feather thickness so it isn't parallel to the main direction.

Checking the cross product confirms either sign works, so I'll make the helper accept arrays and convert as needed. For feathers, I need to attach them to the correct bone along the centerline, and for coverts I'm thinking of offsetting them slightly forward and upward from the main feathers to avoid z-fighting, using a moved frame to preserve bone attachment.

I'll trust that approach despite some risk, then move to wing sweep details, the wrist joint, and confirm the upright-spread rest pose with shoulders mounted to the spine. Claws will be styled as eagle talons.

Now I'm sketching texture assets: a feather card SVG with a leaf shape and midrib dots in two color variants, a flower decal made of rotated concentric petal circles, and a basic eye SVG, while estimating overall body height from wingtip to head.

Then I'm defining the skeleton joints -- jaw, head, and neck chain -- specifying their parent-child relationships, positions, and aim directions, with the neck rising steeply from the spine's last point up toward the head. I'm also setting up the skull geometry as a scaled sphere with its paint material, and positioning the beak's starting point relative to the skull center.

Still writing beak and brow geometry...

Still positioning ring dots...

Confirming frame() accepts point/direction inputs, then working through jaguar ear placement with scaled, flattened spheres for outer and inner ear shapes oriented along the local z-axis, plus planning a sagittal fan of crest feathers at varying angles from a base point.

Writing feather helper function...

Now I'm adding decal placement for flower patterns on the flanks, dorsal dot loops with cycling colors, and banded leg coloring based on position.

I'm also planning toe details for each foot: three small toe segments per leg with golden coloring and claw spikes at the tips.

Then I'm positioning a paw-shaped ellipsoid centered under the foot so the bottom sits near ground level, and checking the toe spikes end close enough to the paw surface. After that I start thinking about how the tail root should sweep from the hips.

Now I'm setting up the tail and spine chains using catmull-rom splines through control points, defining the full color palette as hex constants, and sketching a dotted paint function for texture.

I'm defining the body paint function, using cell noise to create belly markings versus a cream base, blending in pink dots near the underside and continuing the pattern logic elsewhere on the body.

Still defining the ruff ring...

Still writing wing geometry...

Working out the tail feather fan directions using cross products to keep each feather's width perpendicular to its direction in the proper plane. Time to write the actual code now, including the eye rings.
